analysis:
All three changed files are test or fixture code under provider-swift/Tests. There are no production source changes in this batch, so there is no new attack surface, no trust-boundary change and no change to authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or data exposure.

1. EngineV2PrefillGeometryTests.swift (new, 425 lines) tests EngineV2Factory.prefillGeometry, productionSchedulerConfig and makeProductionBuild. It uses tiny in-memory models, with DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 and the KV backend guard path set to /dev/null. It writes no persistent data and touches no real keys, keychain or network. It covers Gemma 4's wide prefill chunk, rollback and opt-in overrides, malformed environment values failing toward the SDK geometry, and saturation at Int.max. Paged ring sizing and the media-block floor are checked, which touches availability and memory-safety properties (T-010, T-029 in spirit). It does not touch the SSD prefix-cache surface in T-041.

2. SegmentedFleetGeometry.swift changes only a doc comment on maximumPrefillChunk.

3. ModelCheckpointStorageSpecificationTests.swift adds two assertions that the checkpoint fixture environment pins prefillChunkKey=512 and stepTokenBudgetKey=2048. This keeps the qualification fixtures from inheriting the new Gemma wide default.

Open questions, outside the supplied evidence:
- The production changes to EngineV2Factory.prefillGeometry (wide chunk, ring sizing from max(chunk, stripe), step-budget coverage of media blocks) are not in this batch. A later pass should check that the wide chunk does not raise activation memory or availability risk beyond what these tests assert.
- The malformed-input fail-toward-SDK behavior depends on that production parser.

No findings.
